children: Consumer staples stocks have generally been supported by the defensive nature of everyday consumer demand, but performance across the sector has remained uneven as investors weigh input costs, pricing power and changing consumer preferences.

Packaged food and personal-care companies, in particular, continue to navigate shifts in volumes, margins and household spending patterns. Against this backdrop, a quantitative list finds only two consumer staples stocks that have maintained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for at least 60 consecutive days.
The list is topped by BellRing Brands, Inc.
, which has maintained a Strong Sell Quant Rating for 316 consecutive days. Vital Farms, Inc.

follows with 204 consecutive days at a Strong Sell rating. The two-stock screen spans packaged foods and meats and personal care products, making it notably narrower than similar screens across other sectors.

The limited number of qualifying names means only two consumer staples stocks have sustained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for more than two months. Both companies have remained at the Strong Sell end of Seeking Alpha's quantitative rating scale for an extended period.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings evaluate stocks using quantitative measures including valuation, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and momentum. Ratings range from 1 to 5, with scores below 2.5 considered Sell or Strong Sell ratings.

title: Only two consumer staples stocks have long-running Strong Sell Quant ratings
